Mr. Sah, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the petitioner no.1 namely Sarvesh Kumar Tiwary and petitioner no.2 Mithlesh Kumar Tiwari have left for their heavenly abode and in view of that, these petitions are confined only to the petitioner namely Kaushlesh Tiwary @ Kaushlesh Kumar Tiwary @ Koushlesh Kumar Tiwari.

sentences.text: Mr. Sah, the learned counsel submits that all these FIRs have been registered for one transaction and unnecessarily five cases have been lodged against the petitioner.
He submits that in view of that, the entire case is required to be amalgamated and in view of that, the proper order may kindly be passed.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsels appearing for the respondent State submits that so far Cr.M.P. No.2531 of 2017, Cr.M.P. No.2591 of 2017 and Cr.M.P. No.2532 of 2017 are concerned, the matter is at evidence stage.
They submit that charge sheet has been submitted and cognizance has been taken and the matter is pending for prosecution evidence.
They submits that in view of that the further development is there, and in view of that, only the FIR is under challenge and these petitions may not be allowed.
They further submits that the transactions are not similar.

The cases have been registered for different roads and the amount of construction are also different and in view of that,
they jointly submit that these are not the cases of amalgamation.
6. Looking to the contents of the F.I.R of different cases, it appears that the amount of contract is different.

The stretch road is also different and in view of that, it cannot be said that these cases are arising out of same transaction and if such a situation is there, all the cases cannot be directed to be tried together and further in some of the cases, the trial is already at advance stage.

In this regard, a reference may be made to Lalu Prasad @ Lalu Prasad Yadav v. State through C.B.I (A.H.D.), Ranchi,
Jharkhand", (2003) 11 SCC 786.
